counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.0043749598682440629 to 0.001 with all else identical; finer integration removes the momentum drift

explanation: Bodies 0 (m~20) and 1 (m~4.1) start ~1.5 apart with G~3.45, producing very strong mutual acceleration. The integrator used only 1 substep per step (substeps_in_step=1 at steps 0-2). Step 1 conserved momentum to roundoff but step 2 changed total momentum by 0.026 (allowed 0.0059) and angular momentum by 0.53. Pairwise symmetric gravity should conserve momentum to roundoff; the drift shows leapfrog truncation error because the substep controller failed to subdivide this strong-interaction step. Reducing dt alone removes the failure.
vision_note: Two small bodies stay nearly overlapping near the right boundary across steps 0, 1 and 2, while a third body remains isolated near the top center with almost no visible displacement. There is no obvious explosion, fast ejection, or wall contact, only a nearly static close pair.
